paper.title_en: Spacetime as a discrete medium: A resolution of the cosmological constant problem
paper.abstract_en: We introduce a model where spacetime is a discrete medium of massive elementary structures. The observed dark energy density <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Λ</mi></mstyle></msub><mo>∼</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.33em"/><mtext>eV</mtext><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></math> emerges naturally when the structures have mass <math altimg="si2.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Λ</mi></mstyle></msub><mo>∼</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.33em"/><mtext>eV</mtext></mrow></math> and separation <math altimg="si3.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Λ</mi></mstyle></msub><mo>∼</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mspace width="0.33em"/><mtext>mm</mtext></mrow></math>, precisely the neutrino mass and cosmological constant scales. The model predicts spatial cosmological constant variation, ultralight particles, and modified gravitational wave propagation, resolving the cosmological constant problem without fine-tuning or anthropics.
